key_insight: Empirical residual minimization for kernels and physics-informed neural networks can be converted into provable pointwise error bounds for Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equations on unbounded domains.
engineering_relevance: This gives a theoretically grounded way to use mesh-free solvers for high-dimensional control and optimization PDEs when classical grid methods are impractical.
method: Wendland-kernel collocation with a native-space norm constraint and fill-distance-dependent convergence.
Physics-informed neural networks with smooth activations and a Sobolev-norm constraint, yielding probabilistic convergence.
Both analyses recover sup-norm residual control from empirical squared loss using interpolation and domain-truncation error estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both uniform convergence results and quantitative a posteriori error bounds, supported by numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions.
watch_item: The convergence guarantees require additional regularity assumptions beyond viscosity well-posedness, so the theory may not apply directly to rough or highly irregular solutions.
paper_title: Convergence of kernel and neural-network methods for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations on unbounded domains
